headline: Tadalafil,
every day.
dek: The research behind daily 5 mg tadalafil, and the finished US trial testing it without a prescription.
photoAlt: A barber in a black smock holds a folded leaflet.
byline: Adonis Men’s Health · Checked Nov 3, 2026 · Clinical review pending

glance.label: Approved uses
glance.line: Daily tadalafil is approved in the US for ED, for BPH symptoms, and for both.

glance.label: The evidence
glance.line: Placebo-controlled trials of 12 to 26 weeks; longer data are open-label.

glance.label: The US switch trial
glance.line: 2,212 enrolled, completed Apr 2026. No results posted yet.

pull.quote: the incremental benefit of CIALIS beyond 26 weeks is unknown.

body: Most men who know [[/tadalafil|tadalafil]], sold as Cialis, know it as a pill taken before sex. Its US label describes a second way to use it: a low dose once a day, “taken at approximately the same time every day, without regard to timing of sexual activity.”[^label] The label lists daily use for erectile dysfunction and for the urinary symptoms of an enlarged prostate, called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH, or for both conditions together.[^label] That daily 5 mg tablet is also what a US trial has just tested for use without a prescription.[^ctg]

The label gives tadalafil a mean half-life of 17.5 hours in healthy men,[^label] and says a single as-needed dose improved erectile function compared with placebo for up to 36 hours.[^label] With daily dosing, one trial team wrote, dosing and sex no longer need to be timed together.[^porst08]

For erectile dysfunction, the label reports two placebo-controlled trials of daily dosing in general groups of men and one in men with diabetes, 853 men in all.[^label] The 24-week US trial enrolled 287 men. On a 30-point erectile function score, 5 mg raised the score by 7.0 points, 2.5 mg by 6.1 and placebo by 1.2; the share of attempts ending in successful intercourse rose 35 percentage points on 5 mg against 10 on placebo.[^label] In a 12-week trial outside the US, 268 men were assigned to placebo, 5 mg or 10 mg; at the end, 51.5% of men on 5 mg reported scores in the no-ED range, against 8.3% on placebo, and nine men (3.4%) stopped because of side effects.[^porst06]

The longer studies were open-label, with no placebo group. In open-label extensions, 234 men took 5 mg daily for one year and 238 for two; 58.4% finished the two-year study, and the authors reported no serious adverse events related to the drug.[^porst08] With no placebo group, they cannot separate drug effect from other causes.

Is daily better than as-needed? A 2013 open-label trial randomized 770 men new to these drugs to tadalafil 5 mg daily, tadalafil 10 mg as needed, or [[/sildenafil|sildenafil]] 50 mg as needed, for 8 weeks, followed by 16 weeks in which men could switch.[^buvat] It measured how long men stayed on their first treatment. An estimated 52.2% stopped daily tadalafil, 42.0% stopped as-needed tadalafil and 66.7% stopped sildenafil, while gains in erectile function did not differ between groups.[^buvat] Several of the authors listed affiliations with Lilly Deutschland,[^hatzi] part of the company that developed Cialis.[^pharmaphorum]

For BPH, two 12-week trials used the International Prostate Symptom Score.[^label] The first randomized 1,058 men to placebo or one of four daily doses; the second, 325 men to 5 mg or placebo.[^label] On 5 mg, scores fell 4.8 and 5.6 points, against 2.2 and 3.6 on placebo, while peak urine flow was not significantly different from placebo.[^label] The first trial’s authors concluded that “Of the doses studied 5 mg tadalafil appeared to provide a positive risk-benefit profile.”[^roehrborn] A 26-week trial of 696 men starting finasteride found the extra benefit of tadalafil shrank from 1.7 points at week 4 to 1.0 at week 26, and the label states that “the incremental benefit of CIALIS beyond 26 weeks is unknown.”[^label]

A third trial took 606 men who had both conditions.[^egerdie] After 12 weeks, 5 mg cut the symptom score by 6.1 points against 3.8 on placebo, and raised the erectile function score by 6.5 points against 1.9; 2.5 mg did not significantly improve urinary symptoms.[^label]

In the 12-week daily ED trials, headache was reported by 6% on 5 mg and 5% on placebo, and indigestion by 5% and 2%; in the BPH trials, headache by 4.1% and 2.3%.[^label] The label is firm on nitrates: “Administration of CIALIS to patients who are using any form of organic nitrate, either regularly and/or intermittently, is contraindicated.”[^label] It also rules out riociguat, a lung blood-pressure drug.[^label] It warns that “Priapism, if not treated promptly, can result in irreversible damage to the erectile tissue.”[^label] It reports rare sudden vision loss and sudden hearing loss with this drug class, citing observational studies of a roughly doubled risk of one eye condition that, it says, do not establish cause.[^label]

The new US trial asks whether men can decide for themselves that the drug suits them. Opella, Sanofi’s consumer health business, said such trials aim to “confirm that consumers can self-diagnose and treat themselves appropriately without the help of a healthcare provider.”[^lift] The study is phase 3, open-label and single-group, run remotely with US residents.[^ctg] Men 18 or older who completed a mandatory digital health survey with a purchase code, and bought the product, moved on to a 120-day use phase of 5 mg daily.[^ctg] Its main measures were whether men kept to the dosing interval, by electronic diary, and whether the survey turned away people a medical assessment said should not use the drug; others tracked whether nitrate users were screened out and whether men sought care for priapism or sudden vision or hearing loss.[^ctg]
It began on January 30, 2025, after FDA lifted a hold placed in 2022,[^lift][^hold] and finished on April 2, 2026, with 2,212 people enrolled.[^ctg] No results have been posted.[^ctg]

As context, an FDA rule effective May 2025 lets a nonprescription drug come with an extra condition such as an online survey, and FDA says: “Right now, there are no FDA-approved nonprescription drugs with an ACNU.”[^acnu] Poland allowed a 10 mg tadalafil without prescription in 2022,[^hbwpl] and in March 2023 the UK made a 10 mg Cialis tablet a pharmacy medicine sold after a talk with a pharmacist.[^mhra]
What remains unknown is mostly about time and self-judgment: the controlled trials ran 12 to 26 weeks, the longer data have no comparison group, and the actual-use results are not public.
